Comprehension of S2.2 (security-reviewer), documents only: docs/design/greenfield-senior.md section 18.0 and the three paragraphs of 18.4/18.5 named by the dispatch.

18.0 (threat model). The runner defends against accidental and LLM-plausible cross-group writes made by project code an agent runs (relative path, absolute path, symlink, git). Deliberate tampering with git internals is out of scope for prevention and left to content-hash detection at integration; OS-level isolation is a named limit (L-GF-40). On the managed path, prevention is the throwaway copy (relative writes land in the copy) and detection is the hash of the real tree (absolute paths, absolute symlinks, git -C), which fails the run without undoing it (L-GF-29). Findings outside the model are listed in a summary and registered as limits; a recorded finding is judged by GF-CLOSE-2 and GF-CLOSE-6 whatever its subject.

18.4, "The copy and the real tree (S2.1)". The wrapper hashes the real tree by walking the file system (content and mode; symlinks by target; git directories included, objects/ by name and size). Since S2.2 (H2-2) the hash also covers .eccode/, except events.jsonl, state.json and config.json (restored by the frozen record window, which fails the run itself), that window's lock files (.lock, .lock.waiting-*) and the tools' caches. It copies the tree without .git and .eccode/ to a temporary directory outside the project, runs the command there with the repository variables removed and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES set, then re-hashes the real tree: a change outside the caller's group, anything inside the git directories and anything inside .eccode/ (drafts, evidence logs, guard configs, artifacts) fails the run with exit 99 and names the paths. Otherwise changes in the copy that the caller's group owns are copied back; others are discarded and listed; nothing under .git or .eccode/ and no cache is ever copied back. The copy-back is inside the frozen integrity window, which can still fail the run without undoing what was copied back (H1-3).

18.4, "The runner is the only route (S2.2, H2-1)". In a Greenfield-Senior project the role-locked server refuses to a group role the frozen command tools (evidence_run, fix_verify, mutate, lab_repro, lab_hypothesis_test, lab_localize, lab_bisect, lab_trace), naming gf_run; the decision is made per call because a project can become Greenfield-Senior after the server starts. The orchestrator and roles in no group keep them. fix_verify and mutate are refused rather than routed because the copy cannot model them. The runner's evidence records the command it ran as `command` (runner.executed keeps the wrapper line), so the frozen completion check accepts a passing runner run of the pinned command as the task's pinned run.

18.5, "Acceptance with limits (GF-CLOSE-6)". When a scope does not close, `user` may commit gf.slice.accepted from the owner CLI only (no MCP tool) with a JSON list of {finding, severity, limit, reason}. Refused unless: actor user; clean tree (bound to HEAD^{tree}); scope neither closed nor already accepted; the list holds exactly every open finding (a finding of any review of the scope without a valid resolution, judged at the acceptance's own seq), each once, with its recorded severity, an L-GF-<n> id and a reason of 30+ characters, nothing else; no listed finding is blocking; the list is not empty. The engine writes a fixed caveat (L-GF-17). Acceptance resolves nothing; the scope stays open and closable; only a second acceptance is refused; the audit replays it and reports it as accepted, not closed.

Findings: one minor documentation finding (I1-1, below): the GF-CLOSE-6 paragraph says a scope that does not close for a non-finding reason (a standing no-go, a missing review step, a battery, the accounting) "cannot be accepted either", but the refusal conditions it lists constrain only the findings list, so a reader cannot tell whether a scope that has open non-blocking findings AND a standing no-go (or a missing step) is accepted, and therefore what an acceptance event asserts about the scope's other closure conditions.

Not findings (outside the S2.2 scope or not contradictions):
- The closing sentence of "The copy and the real tree" says a write that reaches the real tree another way "fails the run and is named, and is not undone"; for the three record files the paragraph itself says the record window puts them back and fails the run. The exception is stated in the same paragraph, so I read the closing sentence as general, not as a contradiction.
- The paragraph does not say whether the run's own evidence log (written into .eccode/ by the frozen runner) is written before or after the wrapper's second hash; if during, every run would fail. This is a code question, checked in the critique, not a contradiction in the text.
- With .eccode/ now hashed, another agent's concurrent write there (its own evidence log, a draft, a handoff) fails this run "as if the run had made it"; the text states this rule, so it is a consequence, not a contradiction.
- The table row for GF-CLOSE-6 does not repeat the empty-list refusal; the paragraph adds it and the two do not conflict.
- "the roles in no group keep the tools" leaves the reviewer roles' grouping to 18.1, which I was not asked to read.
